metadataReview.note: Date this record to the second engagement identified as the Ugeumchi battle by the National Institute of Korean History: lunar 8–11 November 1894, corresponding to Gregorian 4–7 December. The chronology explicitly prints both calendars for 8, 9 and 11 November. This replaces the imported October–November numerical range rather than mixing the earlier Gongju fighting with the named second battle. The chronology mentions scattered retreat continuing around lunar 11–12 November; that does not extend the named four-day battle to every subsequent withdrawal. Add the Korea Heritage Service location of the protected battlefield as a representative sector locator, not a reconstructed troop position.

metadataReview.coordinateBasis: The official Korea Heritage Service entry for Ugeumchi Battlefield, Gongju (historic site 387, 697297 square metres) publishes its position-button parameters as longitude 127.1122867 and latitude 36.43321101. Its paired heritage description identifies the pass below Gyeonjun Mountain as the place where Donghak forces fought the government/Japanese coalition. Round the published location to four decimals. This is a locator of the designated battlefield sector, not an exact point of all fighting, a measured positional error, or the surveyed centre of the 697297-square-metre area. The 1973 memorial is not being used alone to establish the battlefield.

note:
The National Institute of Korean History distinguishes three military actors in two opposing camps: Donghak forces opposed the Joseon government troops and Japanese troops acting together. The latter remain separately identified local forces sharing a camp, not one inferred nationality. The Korea Heritage Service likewise describes the government/Japanese coalition at this battlefield. No strength, deaths, casualties, percentages, troop ratios, equipment profile or equipment identity is supplied; figures quoted for the wider Gongju fighting or later survivors are not converted into Ugeumchi casualties.
